title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions
subtitle: Practical tips for how to run efficient sessions that get the most value from every token.

items.text: Run /clear between tasks. This prevents prior irrelevant context from being sent back to the model, which can reduce token usage.
items.html: Run /clear between tasks. This prevents prior irrelevant context from being sent back to the model, which can reduce token usage.

items.text: Set your model and effort level before you start. Changing either one mid-conversation can bust your prompt cache, which can increase token cost.
items.html: Set your model and effort level before you start. Changing either one mid-conversation can bust your prompt cache, which can increase token cost.

items.text: @-mention files instead of naming them. The file gets attached to your message directly, which saves a Read call, or a search if Claude has to go find it.
items.html: @-mention files instead of naming them. The file gets attached to your message directly, which saves a Read call, or a search if Claude has to go find it.

items.text: Add quiet flags to noisy commands, or run them in a subagent. Command output is added to the conversation just like a file, and stays there for the rest of the session.
items.html: Add quiet flags to noisy commands, or run them in a subagent. Command output is added to the conversation just like a file, and stays there for the rest of the session.

items.text: Run /context once in a fresh session. It shows what's loaded ( CLAUDE.md , MCP tool definitions), so you can cut out anything unnecessary.
items.html: Run /context once in a fresh session. It shows what's loaded (CLAUDE.md, MCP tool definitions), so you can cut out anything unnecessary.

items.text: /compact before you take a break from your keyboard. The prompt cache expires after an hour, and summarizing a conversation is much cheaper while it's still cached.
items.html: /compact before you take a break from your keyboard. The prompt cache expires after an hour, and summarizing a conversation is much cheaper while it's still cached.

blocks.text: Until pretty recently, the tools you wrote code with were a flat fee (or free). Your editor cost the same whether you fixed one test or fifty that afternoon, so an individual task didn't really have a price of its own.
blocks.html: Until pretty recently, the tools you wrote code with were a flat fee (or free). Your editor cost the same whether you fixed one test or fifty that afternoon, so an individual task didn't really have a price of its own.

blocks.text: With agentic coding tools like Claude Code, it does. The same completed task can also cost different amounts depending on how you use it.
blocks.html: With agentic coding tools like Claude Code, it does. The same completed task can also cost different amounts depending on how you use it.

blocks.text: In one session, Claude reads the test and the file it covers, makes the edit, and is done in a handful of turns. In another, it greps around the repo first, reads a dozen files on its way to the same two, and every one of those turns also drags along everything else that's been read into the conversation since this morning.
blocks.html: In one session, Claude reads the test and the file it covers, makes the edit, and is done in a handful of turns. In another, it greps around the repo first, reads a dozen files on its way to the same two, and every one of those turns also drags along everything else that's been read into the conversation since this morning.

blocks.text: It's the same fix, but you spent a different number of tokens on it, and the whole time the model was also having to think about ten files it didn't need.
blocks.html: It's the same fix, but you spent a different number of tokens on it, and the whole time the model was also having to think about ten files it didn't need.

blocks.text: Being efficient with tokens doesn't mean using fewer of them overall. It means making sure the ones you do use go towards the thing you actually asked for.
blocks.html: Being efficient with tokens doesn't mean using fewer of them overall. It means making sure the ones you do use go towards the thing you actually asked for.

blocks.text: So let's look at what decides the price of a token, then what decides how many of them a session sends, and along the way, what that means for how you run a session.
blocks.html: So let's look at what decides the price of a token, then what decides how many of them a session sends, and along the way, what that means for how you run a session.

blocks.text: What decides the price of a token
blocks.html: What decides the price of a token

blocks.text: You're billed per token, but what you're actually paying for is inference: the time it takes a GPU (or a TPU, or whatever the model happens to be running on) to run the model over your tokens.
blocks.html: You're billed per token, but what you're actually paying for is inference: the time it takes a GPU (or a TPU, or whatever the model happens to be running on) to run the model over your tokens.

blocks.text: Three things decide how much of that time a token takes: which model you're running, whether it's an input token (going in) or an output token (coming out), and whether it was cached.
blocks.html: Three things decide how much of that time a token takes: which model you're running, whether it's an input token (going in) or an output token (coming out), and whether it was cached.

blocks.text: A bigger model does more work on both input and output tokens. Which model is worth it for which kind of work is a topic on its own, and we covered it in Choosing a Claude model and effort level in Claude Code .
blocks.html: A bigger model does more work on both input and output tokens. Which model is worth it for which kind of work is a topic on its own, and we covered it in Choosing a Claude model and effort level in Claude Code.

blocks.text: For this post, all you need to know is that everything else we're about to cover gets multiplied by the model's price: use a larger model when the problem is genuinely hard or ambiguous, and a smaller one when the work is routine.
